section_summary: This section covers State Department records from 1932 to 1942 concerning the unauthorized publication and translation of American copyrighted works in Japan, centering on attorney W. Jefferson Davis's campaign regarding his book 'Japan - The Air Menace of the Pacific.' Although the 1905 bilateral treaty with Japan excluded translations, Davis and his attorneys argued that simultaneous publication of serialized chapters in Great Britain established protection under the Berne Convention. The records include policy memoranda urging United States adherence to the Berne Convention, Tokyo Embassy inquiries and protests against pirated scientific textbooks, and Davis's 1942 inquiry regarding satisfaction of claims from impounded Japanese wartime assets.

subfiles.about: Charging file 894.544 to Wallace McClure in the Treaty Division.
subfiles.summary: Charge slip recording the transfer of file 894.544 to Dr. McClure on August 3, 1939.
subfiles.title: Charge Slip for File 894.544

subfiles.about: Charging file 894.544/20 to E.M.
subfiles.summary: Charge slip recording the transfer of file 894.544/20 to E.M. on July 7, 1949.
subfiles.title: Charge Slip for File 894.544/20

subfiles.about: Routing and legal jurisdiction of W. Jefferson Davis's copyright claim against impounded Japanese assets.
subfiles.from: Division of Financial and Disbursing Operations (BMcB / FL)
subfiles.summary: Memorandum discussing routing of Davis's claim against impounded Japanese funds, noting doubts about its validity and referring to the Legal Adviser.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Routing of Davis Copyright Claim

subfiles.about: Transmitting diplomatic note protesting unauthorized Japanese publication of American copyrighted books.
subfiles.summary: Despatch transmitting copy of diplomatic note to Japanese Foreign Minister Togo protesting pirating of American books in Japan.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5993: Pirating of American Books in Japan

subfiles.about: Protesting unauthorized publication and sale of American technical books in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Diplomatic note and annexed list protesting unauthorized Japanese editions of American engineering textbooks and requesting remedial action from Japanese authorities.
subfiles.title: Note No. 1974 Protesting Unauthorized Publication of American Books

subfiles.about: Routing Davis copyright claim correspondence to Legal Adviser official.
subfiles.summary: Routing slip referring correspondence on Davis's copyright claim to Judge Butler for attention.
subfiles.title: Legal Adviser Routing Slip

subfiles.about: Protesting unauthorized translation and sale of Davis's book in Japan and requesting diplomatic assistance.
subfiles.summary: Davis reports unauthorized Japanese publication and large sales of his aviation book, asking whether bilateral reciprocity or Japanese law provides remedies.
subfiles.title: Letter Regarding Unauthorized Publication of Davis Book in Japan

subfiles.about: Advising Davis that international agreements do not provide legal recourse for unauthorized translations in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Informs Davis that under international agreements and Japanese law, no legal recourse exists against unauthorized translations.
subfiles.title: Letter to W. Jefferson Davis Regarding Copyright Recourse

subfiles.about: Instructing the Tokyo Embassy to report on the Japanese publication of Davis's book.
subfiles.summary: Directs Ambassador Grew to forward any available information regarding the Tokyo publication of Davis's translated book.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 144 on Publication of Davis Book

subfiles.about: Reporting findings from an interview with publisher Shinkosha regarding sales of Davis's translated book.
subfiles.summary: Reports that Shinkosha admitted selling roughly 45,000 copies, noting advertised claims of 130 editions were grossly exaggerated.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 257 on Sales of Davis Book in Tokyo

subfiles.about: Inquiring whether the American Consul General at Tokyo has taken action on his copyright protest.
subfiles.summary: Davis inquires whether the Department or Consul General in Tokyo has taken action regarding his copyright protest.
subfiles.title: Letter Inquiring on Status of Copyright Protest

subfiles.about: Communicating Embassy findings on sales figures of the Japanese edition of Davis's book.
subfiles.summary: Informs Davis of the Tokyo Embassy report that Shinkosha sold about 45,000 copies of his book.
subfiles.title: Letter Reporting Embassy Findings on Book Sales

subfiles.about: Explaining that the 1905 bilateral treaty with Japan excludes translations, precluding diplomatic representations.
subfiles.summary: Explains that the 1905 treaty explicitly excludes translations from reciprocal protection, leaving no basis for official representations to Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter Regarding Treaty Exceptions for Translations

subfiles.about: Reviewing 1905 treaty negotiations and submitting a draft reply to Davis.
subfiles.summary: Reviews 1905 diplomatic correspondence proving Japan refused copyright protection for translations, and submits a draft letter for Davis.
subfiles.title: Policy Memorandum No. 651: Copyright Protection of Translations

subfiles.about: Using the Davis case to argue for United States adherence to the Rome revision of the Berne Convention.
subfiles.summary: Argues that Davis's loss illustrates the urgent need for Senate adherence to the Berne Convention, which protects translations and would supersede conflicting domestic statutes.
subfiles.title: Policy Memorandum No. 653: The United States and International Copyright

subfiles.about: Protesting Japanese misuse of his book as anti-American propaganda and transmitting letter to Chester Rowell.
subfiles.summary: Davis protests Japanese military propaganda use of his book, critiques treaty deficiencies, and encloses an open letter answering columnist Chester Rowell.
subfiles.title: Letter to Secretary Hull on Japanese Piracy and Propaganda

subfiles.about: Defending his book on aviation preparedness and warning against Japanese militarism in rebuttal to newspaper criticism.
subfiles.summary: Extended open letter defending the patriotic motives of his aviation book, refuting allegations of jingoism, and detailing Japan's aggressive military and aviation programs.
subfiles.title: Open Letter to Chester H. Rowell on Air Preparedness

subfiles.about: Proposing joint legal action based on British copyright protection for serialized chapters in the Saturday Evening Post.
subfiles.summary: Davis proposes that Curtis Publishing join legal proceedings against Japanese publishers based on British copyright protection for serialized chapters.
subfiles.title: Letter to George Horace Lorimer Proposing Joint Legal Action

subfiles.about: Explaining the omission of protest acknowledgment language in draft reply to Davis.
subfiles.summary: Internal note explaining why the reply omitted acknowledgment of Davis's protest, since he was previously told nothing could be done.
subfiles.title: Department Note on Draft Reply to Davis

subfiles.about: Acknowledging receipt of Davis's letter to Secretary Hull and enclosed letter to Chester Rowell.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Davis's letter of November 6, 1933, and his enclosed open letter to Chester Rowell.
subfiles.title: Letter Acknowledging Correspondence from Davis

subfiles.about: Arguing that simultaneous British publication of a serialized chapter established Berne Convention protection.
subfiles.summary: Davis argues that simultaneous publication of his chapter in Great Britain creates Berne Convention protection against Japanese infringement.
subfiles.title: Letter Arguing Berne Protection via British Publication

subfiles.about: Routing note regarding Davis copyright case.
subfiles.summary: Internal routing slip transmitting memorandum and draft reply in the Davis copyright case.
subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs Routing Slip

subfiles.about: Proposing draft reply stating that Berne Convention rights must be determined in Japanese courts.
subfiles.summary: Recommends informing Davis that whether simultaneous British publication confers protection is a judicial question for Japanese courts requiring private counsel.
subfiles.title: Legal Adviser Memorandum on Reply to Davis

subfiles.about: Draft text advising Davis that copyright claims under international conventions require private counsel.
subfiles.summary: Draft advising Davis that questions of international copyright protection are legal issues requiring private legal counsel.
subfiles.title: Draft Reply to W. Jefferson Davis

subfiles.about: Advising Davis that copyright questions under the Berne Convention must be pursued in Japanese courts through private counsel.
subfiles.summary: Advises Davis that the effect of simultaneous British publication on Japanese copyright is for determination in Japanese courts through private counsel.
subfiles.title: Letter Advising Judicial Recourse in Japan

subfiles.about: Conversation with Davis regarding copyright treaty support and avoiding inflammatory publicity.
subfiles.summary: McClure notes Davis compared his case to 'Gone With the Wind,' urging him against press agitation while Davis contacted senators supporting the treaty.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on Copyright in Japan

subfiles.about: Forwarding Curtis Publishing correspondence and seeking Tokyo Embassy cooperation for Japanese associate.
subfiles.from: Stephen P. Ladas (Langner, Parry, Card & Langner)
subfiles.summary: Ladas reports requesting a publication affidavit from Curtis Publishing and asks that the Tokyo Embassy assist their Japanese associate in negotiations.
subfiles.title: Letter Regarding Evidence of Simultaneous Publication

subfiles.about: Inquiring whether the Saturday Evening Post of October 30, 1926 was published simultaneously in a Berne Union country.
subfiles.summary: Asks Curtis Publishing whether the October 30, 1926 issue was published simultaneously in Great Britain or Canada, requesting an affidavit.
subfiles.title: Letter Inquiring on Simultaneous Publication

subfiles.about: Confirming British copyright protection for all issues of the Saturday Evening Post and offering an affidavit.
subfiles.from: Philip S. Collins (The Curtis Publishing Company)
subfiles.summary: Confirms all Saturday Evening Post issues are copyrighted in Great Britain and offers to execute an affidavit.
subfiles.title: Letter Confirming British Copyright Protection

subfiles.about: Acknowledging Ladas's letter and promising continued Department attention.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Ladas's letter of March 8 and states the Department will give continued attention to the case.
subfiles.title: Letter Acknowledging Law Firm Inquiry

subfiles.about: Reviewing legal aspects of simultaneous publication under the Berne Convention and offering Embassy inquiries.
subfiles.summary: McClure explains treaty hurdles, asks for proof of simultaneous British publication under the Berne Convention, and offers to recommend Tokyo Embassy inquiries.
subfiles.title: Letter on Requirements for Berne Protection

subfiles.about: Instructing Tokyo Embassy to investigate Davis copyright case based on Berne Convention simultaneous publication proof.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Curtis Publishing affidavit proving simultaneous British publication, instructing Embassy to investigate Davis's claim under Berne Convention provisions.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 1501 on Copyright Protection in Japan

subfiles.about: Reporting efforts by Tokyo associate Koh Kawarada and Counsel Mishina to negotiate with publisher Shinko-sha.
subfiles.summary: Informs Davis that Japanese associates are attempting an amicable settlement with Shinko-sha based on British copyright protection.
subfiles.title: Letter to Davis on Settlement Negotiations in Tokyo

subfiles.about: Attesting that the Saturday Evening Post is published simultaneously in the United States and Great Britain.
subfiles.summary: Affidavit by Curtis Publishing Treasurer certifying simultaneous US and British publication of the Saturday Evening Post since 1926.
subfiles.title: Affidavit of C. W. Bok on Simultaneous Publication

subfiles.about: Incomplete copy of letter reporting settlement negotiations in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: First page of law firm letter reporting efforts by Japanese associates to obtain a settlement from Shinko-sha.
subfiles.title: Copy of Letter to Warren Jefferson Davis (Page 1)

subfiles.about: Execution and declaration page of Bok affidavit.
subfiles.summary: Attestation page of C. W. Bok's affidavit executed at Philadelphia under Revised Statutes section 1778.
subfiles.title: Affidavit of C. W. Bok (Page 2)

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of letter reporting settlement negotiations in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Complete duplicate copy of law firm letter reporting settlement efforts by Koh Kawarada and Counsel Mishina.
subfiles.title: Duplicate Letter to Davis on Negotiations in Tokyo

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of letter requesting Curtis Publishing affidavit and Embassy assistance.
subfiles.from: Stephen P. Ladas (Langner, Parry, Card & Langner)
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of Ladas's letter regarding Curtis Publishing correspondence, affidavit preparations, and Tokyo Embassy assistance.
subfiles.title: Duplicate Letter to McClure on Publication Evidence

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of Bok affidavit certifying simultaneous US and British publication.
subfiles.summary: Complete duplicate copy of Bok's affidavit certifying simultaneous publication of the October 30, 1926 issue in England.
subfiles.title: Duplicate Affidavit of C. W. Bok on Simultaneous Publication

subfiles.about: Requesting addresses of Japanese counsel Mishina and associate Koh Kawarada.
subfiles.summary: Embassy requests addresses for Mishina and Kawarada after unsuccessful attempts to trace them in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3145: Addresses in Copyright Case

subfiles.about: Inquiring whether copyright infringement claims against Japan will be paid from impounded wartime assets.
subfiles.summary: Davis asks whether claims machinery will be created to satisfy American copyright claims against Japan from impounded Japanese funds.
subfiles.title: Letter Inquiring on Payment from Impounded Assets
subfiles.to: Stanley K. Hornbeck and Wallace McClure

subfiles.about: Acknowledging Davis's letter of February 4, 1942, and referring it to Department officers.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck acknowledges Davis's letter on copyright claims against Japan, referring it to Dr. McClure and other officers.
subfiles.title: Letter Acknowledging Claims Inquiry

subfiles.about: Advising Davis that no procedure exists for considering private copyright claims against impounded Japanese assets.
subfiles.summary: Hackworth informs Davis that the United States Government has established no procedure to consider or pay private copyright claims from impounded assets.
subfiles.title: Letter on Lack of Procedure for Claims Against Assets

subfiles.about: Reporting difficulty locating Japanese associates and publishers involved in the Davis case.
subfiles.summary: Reports several unsuccessful attempts to trace Japanese individuals concerned with Davis's case without addresses.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3179 on Tracing Contacts in Davis Case
